news.title: 🔴 ALERT — 7-Zip Just Patched a Dangerous Flaw — Update Now
news.excerpt: A serious security hole (CVE-2026-14266) was disclosed in 7-Zip, the free file compressor many folks use. Opening a malicious .7z file or a bad webpage could let an attacker run code on your PC — even drop ransomware. The fix is simple: update 7-Zip to version 26.02 (open 7-Zip, click Help, then Check for Updates).

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — CISA Warns: Hackers Are Actively Exploiting On-Prem SharePoint — Patch Now
news.excerpt: CISA added a critical on-prem SharePoint flaw (CVE-2026-56164) to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalog after active attacks. If your org runs SharePoint on its own servers, patch now and rotate machine keys — or pull outside access until you can.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — New 'CrashStealer' malware hijacks your Mac by faking Apple
news.excerpt: A new macOS infostealer called CrashStealer spreads through fake "Werkbit Setup" sites, impersonating Apple's CrashReporter to steal passwords, browser data, and crypto wallets. If you see "CrashReporter.dmg" in Downloads, don't open it.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday Fixes 570 Flaws, 3 Zero-Days
news.excerpt: Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday is the largest in company history: 570 flaws fixed, including 3 zero-days — 2 already exploited in the wild. If you run Windows, Office, Exchange, or SharePoint, install updates TODAY.

news.title: Six Zero-Days Live: Patch These Now
news.excerpt: Six vulnerabilities are already under active attack today (July 13, 2026) — including flaws in Adobe ColdFusion, Langflow, and a cluster of Joomla extensions. If you run any of those tools, isolate them. Everyone else: stop hitting "remind me later" on updates.

posts.headline: Stop the ads and trackers following you around the web — uBlock Origin is the free blocker that still works on Firefox and Brave
posts.tip: uBlock Origin is a free, open-source content blocker that removes ads, trackers, and YouTube ads from your browsing. Install it free from the **Firefox Add-ons store (addons.mozilla.org)** or **Brave's extension library** — the full version runs great on both. (Chrome users get the limited "uBlock Origin Lite" because of Google's Manifest V3 changes, so Firefox or Brave is the move for the real thing.)
posts.truth: Most people don't realize the "free" internet is paid for by watching you. Every ad network is also a tracking network, and half the junk that bogs down an old machine for years is just that stuff loading in the background. Block the tracker and the page gets lighter, the battery lasts longer, and the creeps learn a lot less about you.

posts.headline: Tired of reusing passwords? KeePassXC is the free offline password manager that never touches the cloud
posts.tip: KeePassXC is a free, open-source password manager that stores everything in one encrypted file on your own machine — no cloud account, no subscription, nothing leaving your PC. Download it free from **keepassxc.org/download** for Windows, Mac, or Linux.
posts.truth: The honest answer is most people's "password system" is one good password reused everywhere. One breach — and there's a fresh one in the news every week — and every account falls like dominoes. A local vault you control beats any "free" cloud service that can itself get hacked. Your passwords in your hands, not somebody's server.

posts.headline: Skip the monthly ChatGPT bill — Jan is the free desktop app that runs AI models on your PC with no internet and no account
posts.tip: Jan is a free, open-source desktop app that downloads and runs AI language models entirely on your own PC — no cloud, no login, no subscription. Get it at **jan.ai** for Windows, Mac, or Linux.
posts.truth: I see this all the time — folks worried their private notes, tax docs, and family letters are being read by some server halfway across the world. With Jan, the model runs in your room. Your data never leaves the machine. For anything sensitive, that's the only way I'd do it, and it costs you nothing but a little disk space.

posts.headline: Stop paying for WinZip — 7-Zip zips, unzips, and encrypts any archive for free
posts.tip: 7-Zip is a free, open-source file archiver that opens ZIP, RAR, and 7z files and can password-protect them with strong AES-256 encryption. Download it free from **7-zip.org**.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize Windows' built-in zip tool is fine for basic stuff but can't open half the archives people email them, and it won't encrypt a thing. 7-Zip opens RAR, ISO, you name it, and locks a file with a password in two clicks. The "free trial" popups in paid archivers are just noise — this does the job better and asks nothing.

posts.headline: Shrink that giant video file — HandBrake converts any clip to a smaller size for free
posts.tip: HandBrake is a free, open-source video converter that shrinks MP4, MKV, and DVD files without losing noticeable quality. Download it free from **handbrake.fr**.
posts.truth: The honest answer is most people are sitting on 2 GB phone videos they can't email, text, or upload because they were never compressed. HandBrake takes that clip down to a tenth the size with no visible difference — and it's the very same tool we run on the bench when someone brings in a phone full of unshareable memories.

posts.headline: Lost laptop? BitLocker can be bypassed in minutes — install the July Windows Update to close the hole
posts.tip: Turn on BitLocker drive encryption (search “BitLocker” in the Start menu, or Settings > Privacy & Security > Device encryption) and install the July 2026 Windows Update at Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates. The patch for CVE-2026-50661 blocks a physical-attack bypass that let someone with brief hands-on access read or change an encrypted drive.
posts.truth: Most people figure BitLocker turns a stolen laptop into a paperweight. It helps — but on an unpatched machine a thief with five minutes and a screwdriver can get around it. Encryption is not a substitute for a strong password and the latest patch. The update that closed this hole shipped July 14, and I still see machines that haven’t pulled it.

posts.headline: Chrome’s July 2026 update closes 382 security holes — update at chrome://settings/help
posts.tip: Open Google Chrome and update it right now: type chrome://settings/help in the address bar (or Menu > Settings > About Chrome) and let it download the latest build. Chrome’s July 2026 releases (150/151) patched close to 400 bugs, including critical code-execution flaws that let a malicious page run code on your PC.
posts.truth: Folks patch their phone the day an update drops but leave Chrome three versions behind for a year. Your browser touches every site you visit — it’s the most exposed program on your computer, and the one most people never update. An old Chrome is an open window.

posts.headline: Florida storm season: an APC Back-UPS keeps your computer alive when the power goes out
posts.tip: Put your computer on an APC Back-UPS battery unit — grab a BE550G or BX series from apc.com or Amazon, or have Onyx install one. It rides through a blackout and soaks the voltage spikes that roll in right after the lights flicker.
posts.truth: I see more dead motherboards and fried power supplies after a storm than from anything else all year. A $60 battery backup beats a $600 board repair every single time, and it’s the one upgrade most North Florida folks skip until the surge does the choosing for them.
